The corporal has a direct effect on prisoner. The private has a direct effect on prisoner. Method 1: We look directly at how the captain correlates with prisoner in general. Method 2: We look at this correlation case by case according to the private. To understand how the captain affects prisoner, is it more correct to use the Method 1 than Method 2?

In causal inference, "how X affects Y" usually refers to the **total causal effect** of X on Y unless specified otherwise (e.g., "direct effect" or "effect independent of mediators"). The total effect is the sum of all causal pathways from X to Y.
